profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose, Santa Clara County, CA) -- likely STACK's SVY01 campus area, not SVY02
profile.reading: This building is one of two adjacent structures that OpenStreetMap contributors have separately mapped and tagged as Stack Infrastructure buildings in San Jose, California, within Santa Clara County, and it is the easternmost of the pair. Its own mapped geometry, an irregular, multi wing footprint spanning roughly 230 by 60 meters with a height of about 5.6 meters, is distinctly different from its companion building about 70 meters to the west, a simple rectangular structure with a height of about 8.5 meters, confirming these are two genuinely separate buildings rather than a duplicate map entry for one structure. Both sit in the Fortune Drive and Trade Zone Boulevard corridor of San Jose, which is the same immediate area where STACK Infrastructure's own site places its SVY01 campus, a 100 megawatt, four building, 19 acre data center campus, rather than the company's separately documented SVY02 campus in Santa Clara, a single 560,440 square foot former Memorex headquarters building rated at 48 megawatts of IT capacity that an earlier pass through this database had linked to these two San Jose buildings. The same immediate neighborhood is also the site of a newer STACK expansion that the City of San Jose's planning department reviewed under the name Trade Zone Park, a 9.8 acre project at 2400 Ringwood Avenue and 1849 Fortune Drive comprising two four story data center buildings totaling about 522,000 square feet, plus an advanced manufacturing building and a 91 megawatt backup generating facility, which cleared City Council review in May 2023. Because the two buildings mapped here are lower rise than the four story buildings described in that 2023 filing, they more plausibly correspond to two of SVY01's four existing buildings than to the newer Trade Zone Park buildings, though public sources do not allow a building by building match with certainty. STACK Infrastructure, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, is a global data center developer and operator with more than 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 markets in the Americas, Asia Pacific, and EMEA. Santa Clara County, which includes both San Jose and Santa Clara, is broadly recognized within the industry as one of the most land, power, and water constrained data center markets in the country, which is part of why STACK's own materials describe Silicon Valley vacancy running consistently below the national average even as the company continues to add capacity there.

profile.research_note: CORRECTION to earlier pass: coordinates (37.4022094,-121.8923868) and companion way 553223628 (37.4025598,-121.893391) both reverse-geocode into San Jose 95131 (Fortune Drive / Trade Zone Blvd corridor), NOT Santa Clara. STACK's SVY02 (48MW, single 560,440sqft building, former Memorex HQ) is in Santa Clara city, a different city from San Jose within the same county, so the earlier identification of these two ways as SVY02 (via a website field pointing to the svy02 URL) appears to be wrong. Official OSM way records (fetched via api.openstreetmap.org) show way 553223629 is a complex 21-node footprint, height 5.58m, bbox approx 233x62m, and way 553223628 is a simple 9-node rectangle, height 8.46m -- genuinely different buildings, not a duplicate pair. City of San Jose planning records document a separate, newer 'STACK Trade Zone Park' EIR project (SCH 2022060141) at 2400 Ringwood Ave / 1849 Fortune Dr: 9.8 acres, two 4-story DC buildings (~522,194 sqft combined), 91MW backup generator capacity, approved May 2023. Because our two OSM ways were mapped Dec 2022 (before that May 2023 approval) and are lower-rise than 4 stories, they more plausibly represent 2 of the 4 existing SVY01 buildings (100MW/19 acres/4 buildings per stackinfra.com) than the newer Trade Zone Park buildings. Could not confirm which of SVY01's lettered buildings (01A-D, 9-36MW each) each way corresponds to. Prior building_sqft=560440 and it_capacity_mw=48 values (attributed to SVY02) are now considered unconfirmed for this specific building and cleared.

reading.body:
This is one of four buildings on Stack Infrastructure's SVY01 campus in San Jose, part of a 100 MW, four-building complex spanning 1.03 million square feet across 19 acres. The operator publishes total campus capacity but not the individual building breakdown, so this facility's specific load cannot be determined from available sources. At a conservative 10 MW per 100,000 square feet typical of modern colocation, the four buildings might house 100 racks per 10,000 square feet, suggesting capacity in the range of 1,000 to 1,500 GPU-dense racks across the campus, though this is an inference only.

SVY01 is one of three Stack Infrastructure campuses in Silicon Valley totaling 150 MW. This single building sits in a region where only 11 of 103 mapped data center facilities publish power capacity figures. The SVY01 campus represents the largest disclosed facility Stack Infrastructure operates in California, and ranks twelfth among all California facilities with published megawatt counts, though the state total of 365 published MW is concentrated in a small number of disclosed sites.

The facility is certified for colocation services on the operator's own pages, though specific tenant names and workload types are not published. SVY01's location in San Jose places it within reach of California's grid infrastructure, though the state context gives no information on power availability, interconnection lead times, or grid constraints at this site. Stack Infrastructure operates 22 markets globally and three Silicon Valley campuses, indicating this campus is part of a larger distributed infrastructure platform rather than a standalone asset.
